'''Bengt Nölting''' (1 May 1962 – 16 September 2009<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://media.ostsee-zeitung.de/images/oz/anzeigen/pdf/6/9/3/000953539601.pdf |title=Death notice |access-date=11 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110821051130/http://media.ostsee-zeitung.de/images/oz/anzeigen/pdf/6/9/3/000953539601.pdf |archive-date=21 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>) was a German physicist and biophysicist who pioneered various methods in [[biophysics]] and engineering. Achievements include studying [[biological macromolecule]]s, the development of [[self-evolving computer program]]s, and the development new energy technologies. From 1994 to 1997 Nölting was scientist at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]] and the [[Cambridge Centre for Protein Engineering]] (UK) where he developed, together with Sir [[Alan R. Fersht]], methods for the high resolution of [[protein folding]].
